title: Molecular hydrogen and osteoarthritis: multi-target mechanisms and therapeutic effectiveness

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Molecular hydrogen and osteoarthritis: multi-target mechanisms and therapeutic effectiveness》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · sec1-p6】Despite accumulating preclinical evidence, clinical translation is hindered by two linked gaps: an incomplete, unified account of H2 mechanisms and major pharmacokinetic challenges in generating and delivering H2 to the joint.22,24,25,26 Therefore, this review aims to (1) synthesize how H2 disrupts the OA pathological network through multi-target mechanisms and (2) critically evaluate how its central limitation, a transient pharmacokinetic profile, is being addressed by next-generation intelligent delivery platforms. We argue that integrating mechanistic understanding with advanced delivery engineering is key to unlocking the clinical potential of H2 as a DMOAD. Figure 1 provides a graphical overview of the pathological network of OA, the major therapeutic actions of H2, and delivery strategies designed to optimize joint exposure. Collectively, this work seeks to provide a solid theoretical and translational framework for developing molecular H2 as a novel class of DMOADs.

【Introduction · sec1-p1】Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common degenerative joint disease worldwide, characterized by progressive articular cartilage degradation, osteophyte formation, and synovial inflammation. It has become a major global public health concern.1 Epidemiological studies estimate that OA affects more than 595 million people worldwide, and its prevalence and burden are rising with population aging and increasing obesity.2,3 This condition not only causes chronic pain and functional disability in patients but also imposes a substantial socioeconomic burden due to escalating healthcare costs.1,3,4

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Molecular hydrogen and osteoarthritis: multi-target mechanisms and therapeutic effectiveness》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Toward an Integrated Translational Roadmap: from Hydrogen Administration to Exposure-Designed Therapy · sec25-p1】To bridge the gap between preclinical promise and clinical reality identified, the field must undergo a paradigm shift: moving from simple “hydrogen administration” to exposure-designed H2 therapy.24,26 The literature suggests that efficacy is not merely a question of biology, but of physics, specifically, the challenge of maintaining therapeutic residence in a highly diffusive joint environment.50 Therefore, successful translation will require an integrated roadmap that co-develops exposure-designed delivery systems, rational “Hydrogen+” combination strategies, and biomarker-guided patient stratification.33,65 From a practical standpoint, existing OA-oriented H2 delivery approaches can be grouped into five categories with distinct implementation trade-offs (Figure 5).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Molecular hydrogen and osteoarthritis: multi-target mechanisms and therapeutic effectiveness》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Reinterpreting “negative” findings · sec22-p1】Within the exposure-designed framework proposed in this review, such outcomes should not be interpreted as a failure of the mechanistic potential of H2, but rather as a confirmation of a pharmacokinetic mismatch. Systemic administration (e.g., inhalation or oral intake) is unlikely to produce a sustained, quantifiable concentration–time profile in synovial fluid. Such exposure is likely required to engage redox-sensitive pathways at the avascular cartilage interface.24 The “failure” to alter disease progression in early trials is, therefore, an expected consequence of insufficient local target engagement rather than a lack of biological efficacy.24,35

【Conclusion · sec30-p1】H2 is a distinctive therapeutic candidate for OA, as it quenches cytotoxic radicals and modulates downstream redox-sensitive networks governing inflammation, regulated cell death, and matrix metabolism.21,23,71 This multi-target, “network-level” mechanism aligns precisely with the multifactorial nature of OA.65 While mechanistic plausibility is well-established, the primary translational challenge lies in ensuring controlled delivery that maintains effective intra-articular exposure.25,26 Early clinical trials have underscored this pharmacokinetic hurdle, revealing a critical disconnect between route of delivery and sustained target engagement.35
